record.name: St. Vincent de Paul - Madison (charitable assistance)
record.administeredBy: Society of St. Vincent de Paul - Madison (nonprofit)
record._categoriesNote: Spans a food pantry, a charitable pharmacy, clothing and furniture vouchers, microlending, and homelessness prevention -- no single CATEGORY covers it.
record.summary: A drive-through food pantry, a free charitable pharmacy, clothing and furniture vouchers from its thrift stores, small-dollar microloans, and the St. Elizabeth Ann Seton program to help prevent family homelessness. Does not provide rent assistance.
record.benefit: Food, prescription medicine, clothing and household-goods vouchers, small debt-consolidation loans, and case-managed homelessness-prevention help.

steps: Call (608) 257-0919 between 8:00 am and 4:30 pm Monday-Friday, or visit a program directly.
For the drive-through food pantry, come during open hours -- no referral described.
For rent help specifically: SVdP does not offer it; they refer to Dane County's Emergency Assistance Grant and the Tenant Resource Center.

eligibility.note: No published eligibility rule. The site states 'All assistance is provided without regard to someone's religion, race, gender, documented status, ethnicity or age' and describes the programs, but publishes no income test, no geographic rule, and no application criteria. Practically the pantry and pharmacy serve people in need in the Madison area; the specifics are set at intake and by the local conference/volunteers.
eligibility._label: Contact St. Vincent de Paul - Madison to ask what help you may qualify for.

unencodable: Everything. The source publishes no rule to encode. Any income or residency condition applied at intake is undocumented.
Program mix varies (food, pharmacy, vouchers, microloans, Seton program) and each may have its own unpublished practice.

surprises: The most useful thing on the page for a benefits tool is a NEGATIVE: 'We do not provide rent assistance' plus two specific referrals. A record that only captured 'SVdP helps people in need' would send rent-seekers to a dead end; the honest record has to carry the 'not this, try these instead' signal.
